Reaching this developmental milestone is associated with a corresponding wet weight at puberty of 332.3 grams [Wwp = 332.3 grams], reflecting the significant somatic investment required before reproductive activity can be initiated. Individuals that achieve this length typically occupy the top predator niche within their local fish assemblages, preying extensively on smaller teleosts and macroinvertebrates. The pronounced size range between pubertal and ultimate lengths highlights a protracted period of post-maturation growth, a pattern commonly observed in iteroparous neotropical cichlids where continued somatic expansion confers advantages in competitive interactions and fecundity.
